articles.title: Hackers Use ARTEX AI to Steal Azure Key Vault Secrets Just 5 Minutes After Scanning GitHub
articles.summary:
Microsoft says threat actors are using an AI tool called ARTEX to find secrets in public GitHub code and use them against cloud accounts. In one case, the AI agent went from searching GitHub to pulling data from Azure Key Vault in only five minutes. ARTEX AI Azure Key Vault secrets Searching public code for […]

articles.title: Hackers Deploy ArmorSteal Malware Through Fake Software Downloads to Steal Credentials and Mine Crypto
articles.summary:
Hackers are spreading a Python-based malware kit called ArmorSteal through fake software download pages. The kit steals passwords, crypto wallets and Discord accounts, and it also mines Monero in the background. articles.title: Veeam Warns Critical 9.8 Linux Kernel Flaw Could Crash Backup Appliances and Disrupt Recovery Operations
articles.summary:
Veeam warned that a critical Linux kernel flaw with a CVSS score of 9.8, could cause denial of service or memory corruption across backup and recovery products. Veeam’s November 6 impact statement identified a Linux kernel use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-98432) in TCP/IPv4 connection setup and outlined update paths for affected systems. articles.title: U.S. Agencies Warn of Hackers Targeting Industrial Refrigeration to Disrupt Food and Medicine Storage
articles.summary:
CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA, and DOT have warned that hackers are targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems worldwide, putting food, medicine, and other temperature-sensitive goods at risk. The November 5, 2026, warning urges operators to secure exposed controllers before attackers can change temperatures, damage equipment, or disrupt storage operations. The joint federal fact […]

articles.title: Hackers Begin Exploiting OpenSSH SSHole Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
articles.summary:
Attackers have started targeting the SSHole authentication bypass affecting certain OpenSSH servers, according to new SANS Internet Storm Center findings. The flaw allows remote attackers to access some password-disabled Linux accounts by submitting an unusually long password, without knowing valid credentials or holding an SSH key.
